fields.description:
Reduce rebar tickets-store growth and reclaim the ~1 GiB already spent, by making the
reconciler's committed `.bridge_state` cache cheap instead of re-homing it.

Measured facts, full research trail and the three corrected false premises: session_log
**1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (dinky-frowsy-woodborer). Supersedes the tabled plan in
**bronze-used-foxhound** (e594-e1d0). Umbrella: **1270-b740**.

## Context

The `tickets` branch is **1.04 GiB**; **92%** is the reconciler's `.bridge_state` cache, not
ticket data (events are 55 MB). Diffing consecutive committed revisions of `bindings.json`
(1509 bindings) shows the growth is bookkeeping nothing reads:

| field | entries changed per pass |
|---|---|
| `baseline` (the value) | **0** |
| `baseline_advanced_at` (written at `binding_store.py:375`, read nowhere in `src/`) | **1144** |
| `last_get_pass` (rotation bookkeeping) | **20** |

A scattered edit across a sort-ordered 18 MB file defeats git delta compression. Measured on 40
consecutive real revisions rebuilt in a clean repo and repacked `--window=250 --depth=50`, true
marginal cost per version is **12.79 KB** today, **1.74 KB** after deleting the timestamp (7.4x),
and the version count halves once rotation bookkeeping moves out (12.8x total).

## Approach and why this one

Keep the cache committed and make it cheap. `.bridge_state` must stay on-branch because the
reconciler runs on **ephemeral** GitHub-hosted runners, so durable state has to live in git. An
earlier design wrote prev to the main-branch worktree, so prev was always `{}` and the differ
re-derived 2050+ inbound creates every pass (`reconcile.py:258-259`). Epic `6c9c` evaluated and
dropped re-homing it off-branch because the convergence loop already self-heals binding drift.
The levers are content and churn, not location.

The one-time reclaim of existing history is included under an operator-approved quiescence
protocol. Its mechanics are proven: a length-aware
`git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` pipeline on the real branch produced
1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%) while preserving all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges.
The dynamic re-add restores the current `.bridge_state` files, so the rewritten HEAD tree is
**exactly byte-identical** to the recorded pre-rewrite tip tree; only historical versions of the
target paths are removed. Stock git plumbing is used because it is already available and proven
for this repository, avoiding a new third-party core dependency. `git-filter-repo` could preserve
empty commits with `--prune-empty=never`; DAG preservation is therefore not a reason to reject it.

## Scope (children, in dependency order)

1. **A1** delete `baseline_advanced_at` and add the write-when-changed guard in `set_baseline`.
2. **A4-1** fence `bridge_fsck` before `prev_snapshot.json` is narrowed (independent of A1).
3. **A2-1** move `last_get_pass` to `.bridge_state/get_rotation.json`; write both formats and
   read `max(new, legacy)`.
4. **A3** text-normalize baseline description/status/priority, deliberately excluding assignee.
5. **A2-2** delete the legacy inline `last_get_pass` field only after its rollout gate clears.
6. **A4-2** narrow `prev_snapshot.json` to a key-set after A4-1; record forward and reverse corpus
   mutation diffs before merge.
7. **A4-3** suppress branch-3 mutations whose effective Jira payload is empty.
8. **A5** record all committed-format changes, mixed-version rules, and rollback boundaries in
   an ADR after A3 and A4-2 establish the final shapes.
9. **A6-0a** add the fail-closed store-epoch guard at both union sites after A2-2 and A4-3.
10. **A6-0b** make the persistent review-bot clone self-converge and fix its deploy trigger; it
    ships with A6-0a so an `src/rebar/` change activates the deploy path.
11. **A6-0c** build and dry-run the stock-git history-strip tooling after A2-2 and A4-3.
12. **A6-0d** enumerate/delete ref pins and create/verify the off-repo backup bundle after A6-0c.
13. **A6-1** execute the reclaim last, only after A1-A5 and A6-0a..0d are closed and Epic B's B6
    is closed.

### Observable rollout gates

**A2-2 has no fixed-delay gate.** A completed `reconcile-bridge.yml` run must execute at a SHA
descending from the A2-1 merge, and the host probe binary must be explicitly refreshed from a
descendant build with its executable/version and absence of older reconcile processes recorded.
A2-2 retains `max(sidecar, legacy)` read compatibility: any legacy writer output is migrated into
the sidecar and scrubbed on the next new pass, so direct evidence plus self-healing replaces the
former 24-hour proxy.

**A6-1 has no fixed-delay gate.** Before publication, every writer is quiesced; the completed
reconciler workflow SHA must descend from A6-0a; the deployed review-bot runtime and the explicitly
refreshed host runtime must each refuse an epoch mismatch in real-clone probes; and A6-0b must record
the review-bot deployment receipt and persistent-clone convergence. Older binaries ignore the epoch,
so direct behavioral proof from each deployed runtime is mandatory. The operator-attested
zero-session/MCP-stop and bundle requirements remain additional gates.

## Compatibility and rollback

Three committed-format changes share one store file. A2-1 is reversible because it continues
writing the legacy field. A3 is reversible because the read path canonicalizes both shapes
idempotently. A2-2 stops legacy writes and scrubs the field but retains the mixed-version read seam:
a later inline stamp is promoted into `get_rotation.json` before removal. Its direct workflow/host
deployment evidence and old/new-writer integration oracle replace elapsed time. A4-2 requires both
the forward full->key-set corpus diff and the reverse key-set->full rollback diff before merge. The
epoch value is introduced only by the reclaim commit, after the descendant workflow and both live
writer runtimes have directly demonstrated fail-closed epoch behavior under quiescence.

Post-publish rollback

Post-publish rollback is an explicit second quiesced window, not an application-level union:

1. Disable both reconciler workflows, pause the review-bot/autodeploy writers, poll for no in-flight
   runs and an empty Gerrit review queue, and obtain the operator's zero-session/stopped-MCP
   confirmation again.
2. Verify the off-repo bundle, unbundle it into a fresh unfiltered scratch clone, and verify that
   the recorded old tip and deleted tag tips resolve exactly.
3. Restore the old `tickets` tip with `--force-with-lease=<rewritten-tip>:<old-tip>`. This direct,
   operator-controlled ref replacement does not run the application merge guards. Never bypass
   an epoch mismatch inside `sync._union_merge` or `push.py`.
4. Reset/reclone every writer (shared local tracker, review-bot EBS clone, and ephemeral workflow
   worktrees) to the restored tip before re-enabling writes. New-epoch clones must be replaced;
   their mismatch refusal is the safety signal, not a condition to override.
5. Re-run tree/count/identity checks, then re-enable writers in the same order as the forward path.

This makes the bundle executable as recovery while preserving fail-closed behavior in ordinary
clients. A6 remains intentionally non-resumable; all graph assertions run on the scratch clone
before either forward or rollback publication.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Before A2-2 closes, its descendant workflow evidence, explicit host refresh, and
      mixed-version self-healing oracle are recorded. **[operator-attested rollout evidence]**
- [x] Before reclaim publication, the descendant workflow ancestry result plus live review-bot and
      exact host-runtime epoch-refusal probes are recorded. **[operator-attested rollout evidence]**

- [x] Marginal packed cost per changed `bindings.json` version is **<=25% of the pre-change
      baseline measured by the same method** (N>=40 consecutive revisions in a clean repo,
      repack `--window=250 --depth=50`, compute `(pack_N - pack_1)/(N-1)`). Baseline: 12.79 KB.
- [x] Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state produce byte-identical
      `bindings.json` and create no commit. Tier: stateful integration asserting bytes and commits.
- [x] `baseline_advanced_at` is absent from every entry written by `set_baseline`, and no `src/`
      reference remains.
- [x] `rebar reconcile-check` against a pre-migration store leaves the worktree byte-identical.
- [x] A dict-shaped baseline through live `compute_update_fields` matches its normalized-string
      equivalent, and stored description/status/priority are scalars while assignee stays raw.
- [x] Full-prev versus key-set-prev corpus mutation diff over >=4 real snapshot pairs has zero
      delta in non-empty effects reaching Jira; the reverse-direction diff is recorded too.
- [x] `outbound_differ.py` remains <=800 LOC under the locked module-size gate.
- [x] A fresh unfiltered `tickets` clone is <=150 MB; rewritten `HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded
      pre-rewrite tip tree after the dynamic re-add; commit and merge counts are unchanged.
- [x] Before publication, a synthetic post-rewrite writer test in temporary real clones pushes a
      representative review-bot ticket commit, then proves `merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      <new-tip>` is false and incremental `size-pack` growth is <1 MB. Tier: repo integration.
- [x] After the first real post-window review-bot write, the same ancestry and size checks are
      recorded as a ticket comment with old tip, new tip, Gerrit change/vote identifier, command
      exits, and measured byte growth. **[operator-attested post-deploy observation]**
- [x] A stale-epoch clone aborts without a merge at both `sync._union_merge` and `push.py`'s non-FF
      retry, including the complete absent/present/corrupt epoch matrix and operator-visible log.
- [x] The ADR enumerates all format changes, mixed-version protocol, A2-2 gate, and rollback limits.
- [x] The off-repo backup bundle exists and `git bundle verify` passes. **[operator-attested]**
- [x] Operator confirms zero active sessions and all `rebar-mcp` servers stopped before the
      reclaim window. **[operator-attested]**
